title: Percentile Rank of Exam Scores
description:
Calculate the percent rank of each student's exam score — the fraction of students who scored strictly lower than this student.

**Table: exam_results** — `student_id`, `name`, `score`

Output columns: `name`, `score`, `pct_rank`. Order by `score` DESC.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE exam_results (student_id INT, name VARCHAR, score INT); INSERT INTO exam_results VALUES (1,'Alice',95),(2,'Bob',88),(3,'Carol',92),(4,'Dave',78),(5,'Eve',88),(6,'Frank',65),(7,'Grace',72),(8,'Henry',95),(9,'Iris',80),(10,'Jake',55);
solution_sql: SELECT name, score, ROUND(PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score), 4) AS pct_rank FROM exam_results ORDER BY score DESC

test_cases.description: 10 students; top scorers have pct_rank=1.0, bottom scorer has pct_rank=0.0

hints: PERCENT_RANK() = (rank - 1) / (total_rows - 1); the lowest value always gets 0.0 and the highest gets 1.0.
Equal scores receive the same PERCENT_RANK value since they share the same rank.
explanation: PERCENT_RANK() computes (rank-1)/(N-1) where N is total rows. Jake (score 55) gets 0.0 and Alice/Henry (score 95) get 1.0. Bob and Eve both score 88 and share the same PERCENT_RANK value. This function is useful for comparing an individual score to the entire distribution.
